findings.title: Login-cache invalidation uses org-wrapped isEnabled()
findings.body: update() passes the model from getById() into registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(). With organizations enabled, getById() returns an anonymous IdentityProviderModel whose isEnabled() is false when the organization is missing, disabled, or the organization provider is off, even if the stored IdP is enabled. LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() calls that override. If the organization is disabled, an IdP that is already in the getForLogin cache looks ineligible, and an update that also fails the predicate for a real reason (hideOnLogin, linkOnly, or kc.org.broker.public set to false) hits the early return and does not invalidate .idp.login.*. Organization enable/disable does not invalidate those keys either, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only rechecks isEnabled(), not hide-on-login, link-only, or broker-public. After the organization is enabled again, getForLogin still returns that IdP and the login page can show a link-only or non-public organization broker. Compare storage flags (or always invalidate when the stored IdP is or was login-eligible), and re-apply the login predicate when serving cached ids.

findings.title: Login-cache test never deletes the IdPs it creates
findings.body: testCacheIDPForLogin registers cleanup with testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove (same mistake again at the hide-on-login IdP around line 425). The providers are created as idp-alias-0 … idp-alias-20, so this resource does not refer to them and they are left in the shared test realm. A second run, or any later test that counts realm or login IdPs, will see the leaked brokers and the exact size assertions (5, 6, 10, 11) will fail.
